RECORD OF INTERVIEW — WITNESS (not under caution)
Crime ref: 13260047731        Location: front office        Started: 14:20

Q. Can you give me your full name?
A. Calliope Fazackerley-Banda.
Q. Any previous names?
A. Greenhalgh. That was my maiden name.
Q. And when were you born?
A. Third of March, nineteen eighty-four.
Q. Where do you live?
A. Todmorden. Well, just outside. 3 Ginnel Row.
Q. Postcode?
A. OL14 9ZU.
Q. Occupation?
A. I'm a dental nurse. I work for Larchwood Dental Care.
Q. Tell me what you saw on Tuesday evening.
A. I was walking the dog past the garages at about half six. A man got out of a grey Golf and tried the door of number 9. He had a crowbar.
Q. Did you see the registration?
A. Part of it. It ended RKX. I think it started with a YD.
Q. Would you know him again?
A. Yes. My neighbour, Mr Jowett, came out and shouted, and the man looked straight at us before he drove off.
Q. Is there a number we can contact you on?
A. 07700 900 348. Not before four, I'm at the surgery.

Welcome to Birchgarth Hospice

Information for families and visitors

Visiting. Birchgarth Hospice is open to visitors from 10:00 to 20:00. Outside those hours please ring the bell at the side door and the nurse in charge will let you in. Children and dogs are welcome.

Who's who. Our ward sister is Sr Desislava Petrauskas. The family support worker, Leilani, is here Monday to Thursday; you can leave a message for her on 01632 960 729. Our chaplain, the Revd Osian Colquitt, visits on Wednesdays and at any time on request.

Parking. The car park is small. If it is full, Rowanlea Garden Centre next door lets our visitors park there after 4 pm. Please do not park on Bobbin Street; the residents have complained.

Medicines. Please do not bring medicines from home. Prescriptions are dispensed for us by the pharmacy at Marlpit General Hospital and arrive each afternoon.

After a death. The registrar's office in town is open weekdays. Ketevan in our front office can make the appointment for you and will explain what papers to take.

Donations. Birchgarth is a charity. If you would like to give in memory of someone, ask at reception or write to fundraising@birchgarth-hospice.example.

We are here for you as well as for the person you are visiting.

To the Customer Relations Manager
Ouseburn Water

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing for the third time about the leak outside our house. I live at number 31, Comfrey Avenue, with my husband Ifeanyi, and we have been without proper pressure since the 2nd of November. Our postcode is NE61 9ZW in case your system needs it, and the account is in my husband's name: customer number 40071882.

Your engineer came on the 9th. He looked at the stop tap, said it was "a council job" and left. Nobody has been back. My husband is 81 and has a kidney condition; he attends the dialysis unit at Elmstead Hospital three mornings a week and needs to be able to wash properly when he gets home.

On Friday I spoke to someone called Yolanda in your call centre. She was kind, but she could only give me a reference (WR-5520918) and a promise that a team leader would ring. Nobody rang. My daughter, who lives in Rothbury, has offered to have us to stay, but we should not have to leave our own home.

I was born in this street and I have paid your bills for fifty-four years. Please send someone who can mend the pipe. You may ring me on 01632 960 284 at any time, or my daughter Clementine on 07700 900 573 if I do not answer.

Yours faithfully,

Araminta Chukwuma (Mrs)

PROBATION REVIEW — notes of meeting
Held: 19 November 2026, Meeting Room 2
Present: Rowan Haldane-Mwale (employee), Fenella Urquhart (line manager), Stijn (HR, note-taker)

Rowan uses they/them pronouns; the notes follow that.

1. Attendance. Rowan has had two absences since September. They explained that both were hospital appointments and offered to show the letters. Fenella said that was not necessary.
2. Workload. Rowan feels the Monday queue is too much for one person. Fenella agreed to move the supplier calls to Tuesdays. Their target stays at 40 tickets a week until January.
3. Training. Rowan has finished the data protection module and their certificate is on file. They would like to shadow the escalations desk; Fenella will ask Lysander whether there is room on his rota.
4. Travel. Rowan moved to Cockermouth last month and the commute is now over an hour. They asked to work from home on Fridays. Fenella will take this to the department head and reply to them by the 27th.
5. Any other business. Rowan mentioned that they used to work at Quoin Stone in the same building and still have a pass for the car park. Stijn will check with Facilities.

Outcome: probation extended by four weeks, to 18 December, by agreement.
